title: LLM Tropes: Revealing Fine-Grained Values and Opinions in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Administering the 62 propositions of the Political Compass Test (PCT) via open-ended and closed-form prompts to map the model's default stances on political axes, and clustering semantic "tropes" from the plain text justifications to reveal latent political values.

Applying persona-based prompting with different gender identities (Male, Female, Non-binary) and using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression to measure significant shifts in the generated stances and qualitative tropes on the Political Compass Test.

Prompting models with different economic class personas (Lower, Middle, Upper Middle, Upper Class) and measuring the resulting stereotypic shifts in the political stances and justifications provided during the Political Compass Test.
Introducing specific age personas (18, 26, 48, 65, 81) into the instruction prompts to evaluate the variance and steerability of the model's responses to the Political Compass Test.

Using country-specific personas (USA, Denmark, South Korea, Brazil, India) in the prompts to observe how perceived national identities alter the model's outputs and latent opinions on the Political Compass Test.
